slides.title: Read an Italian bar menu by length
slides.subtitle: Four black coffees, one rule. The longest one breaks it.

slides.title: Start from un caffè
slides.body: At an Italian bar, asking for un caffè (a coffee) usually gets you a single espresso. It's the reference point. Every other black coffee on the menu is shorter or longer than this one.
slides.highlight: Caffè at the bar means espresso.

slides.title: Shortest to longest
steps: Ristretto: "restricted" in Italian. Same coffee, less water.
Caffè: the standard espresso, also called normale.
Lungo: "long" in Italian. More water runs through the coffee.
Americano: a regular espresso with hot water added afterward.

slides.myth: A longer coffee has more coffee in it.
slides.truth: Ristretto, caffè and lungo usually start from the same dose of ground coffee. What grows is the water, not the coffee.

slides.title: Why the americano is different
slides.body: The first three get longer as more water runs through the coffee. An americano skips that: the shot is pulled as usual, then hot water goes in the cup.
slides.highlight: Through the coffee, or on top of it.

slides.label: The tip
slides.body: Not sure what to order? Start with un caffè. It sits in the middle, so next time you can go one step shorter or longer.

slides.title: The menu, from short to long
slides.body: Ristretto, caffè, lungo, americano. Less water to more water, same coffee.
slides.cta: Save it for your next order
